text:
The text contrasts the theme of inherent human evil with the theme of societal corruption. In William Golding's *Lord of the Flies*, the presentation suggests that humans are naturally savage and that civilization is a fragile veneer that can easily be stripped away, revealing an innate darkness. Conversely, Jean-Jacques Rousseau’s philosophy presents the opposite view: that humans are naturally good and free, and it is the structures of society that impose corruption and constraint. While both texts address the nature of humanity and its relationship with order, they differ fundamentally in their starting point—Golding sees order as a loss of natural state, whereas Rousseau sees societal order as a loss of natural freedom.

The organ that pumps blood is the heart.
